title: 2003 HMMT February Calculus Problem 2
statement: A particle moves along the \(x\)-axis in such a way that its velocity at position \(x\) is given by the formula \(v(x)=2+\sin x\). What is its acceleration at \(x=\frac{\pi}{6}\) ?

solutions.text:
\(5 \sqrt{3} / 4\)
Acceleration is given by \(a=\frac{d v}{d t}=\frac{d v}{d x} \cdot \frac{d x}{d t}=\frac{d v}{d x} \cdot v=\cos x \cdot(2+\sin x)=5 \sqrt{3} / 4\).
